decisions.title: Encore! Encore!
decisions.situation: You bang a spoon on a bowl. It makes a brilliant noise. You would like to check that result another twenty times.

choices.label: Give the full concert
Try a different rhythm
Look inside the bowl

result.title: A short, loud career
result.body: You keep banging until you drop the spoon. You look very pleased with yourself.

journal.text: I discovered how much noise a spoon and a bowl could make.

decisions.title: Urgent correspondence
decisions.situation: You draw a letter and slide it into a cardboard box. It comes straight out of the missing bottom. The postal service is extremely fast.

choices.label: Fold a bottom for the box
Make a pile for each colour
Send the same letter again

result.title: Delivery delayed
result.body: The letter stays inside this time. You open the box to make sure it arrived.

journal.text: I repaired my cardboard postbox so letters would stay inside.

decisions.title: Imaginary friend wanted
decisions.situation: Freddie is alone at break. They say their imaginary friend has moved to a better school. They are interviewing replacements on the empty part of the bench.

choices.label: Help interview the invisible applicants
Apply, despite being inconveniently real
Pretend you have accidentally sat on one

result.title: A crowded bench
result.body: You reject the first applicant for imaginary biting. Freddie rejects the second for actually being a dragon. You run out of break before making an appointment.

journal.text: I helped Freddie interview replacements for an imaginary friend.

decisions.title: Hostile snack takeover
decisions.situation: Freddie offers a plain cracker for your favourite snack. They call the cracker “rare”. There are twelve more in the packet.

choices.label: Demand two snacks for your one
Eat your snack during the sales pitch
Split yours and spare the cracker

result.title: The negotiator gets greedy
result.body: Freddie nearly agrees, then notices you smiling. They withdraw the cracker and their goodwill.

journal.text: I tried to turn Freddie’s snack offer into a better deal for myself.

decisions.title: Unlimited dragons, limited shelf space
decisions.situation: At the library, you find a book so big you need both arms to carry it. The return desk suddenly looks very far away.

choices.label: Commit to the enormous book
Find a smaller story you love
Ask the librarian for a recommendation

result.title: An ambitious loan
result.body: You finish some of it, skip a confusing chapter, and learn three words you immediately misuse.

journal.text: I borrowed the largest book I could carry.

decisions.title: They do not find it funny
decisions.situation: Someone keeps making a joke out of Freddie’s name. Freddie has stopped correcting them.

choices.label: Use their name properly and speak up
Check on Freddie privately
Join in for a laugh

result.title: A little backup
result.body: You say it is getting old. Freddie thanks you later.

journal.text: I backed Freddie when someone kept mocking their name.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Freddie plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of
Trade one song each
Give a brutally concise review

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Freddie.

journal.text: I listened to Freddie’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: The unpaid goblin
decisions.situation: Freddie turns your group presentation into a pitch for an imaginary company. You are listed as “unpaid goblin”. Their dog is CEO. Grace asks where the actual research is.

choices.label: Open the real research before the dog gets a salary
Whisper a demand for a better job title
Delete the pitch while they are presenting it

result.title: Goblin saves the meeting
result.body: You present your actual work. Grace marks it while Freddie clicks past a slide about office beanbags. The dog receives no academic credit.

journal.text: I rescued our group presentation after Freddie replaced the research with a fake company pitch.

decisions.title: Fastest toy car alive
decisions.situation: You invented the numbers for a marked science report. Your toy car apparently reached 90,000 kilometres an hour. Grace asks to see the original measurements.

choices.label: Admit it and take the report back
Offer a live demonstration instead
Invent a second sheet of measurements

result.title: The car has been recalled
result.body: Grace lets you submit a properly measured replacement with a reduced mark. The real car rolls under a cupboard. You record that too.

journal.text: I admitted inventing science data and replaced my report with real measurements.

decisions.title: Your stand-in has a meeting
decisions.situation: To dodge chores, you left a dummy in your dressing gown at your desk. Freddie is now giving it a serious talk about responsibility. The dummy is handling it well.

choices.label: Step out and take over the discussion
Leave a second dummy to play Freddie
Stay hidden and let the dummy handle it

result.title: A noticeable improvement in posture
result.body: Freddie says the dummy already agreed to take the rubbish out. You do it while the dummy remains at the desk, apparently thinking about its future.

journal.text: I replaced a dummy during Freddie’s lecture and did the chore it had agreed to.

decisions.title: Do teenagers smell fear?
decisions.situation: Freddie asks you to fix their phone. An open draft says, “Do teenagers smell fear? Mine only appears when the fridge opens.” They suddenly offer to fix it themselves.

choices.label: Offer an answer from a qualified teenager
Fix it without mentioning the draft
Send their contacts a mocking reading of it

result.title: Mostly, we smell cheese
result.body: Freddie laughs and admits they were having a moan. You fix the phone, then both turn towards the sound of the fridge opening.

journal.text: I caught Freddie complaining about me and answered their question about teenagers.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Invent a chair-based version
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Suggest improving the flavour first
Praise how neatly it broke
Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Drink the tap water
Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Return the microphone immediately
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

decisions.title: Discreet volunteers wanted
decisions.situation: You post a request for cleanup volunteers in a community chat. Your phone attaches an old shopping list: bleach, bin bags and cable ties. Someone replies, “What exactly are we cleaning?”

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup
Delete the post without explaining
Add “No questions. Bring gloves.”

result.title: The photographs help
result.body: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.

journal.text: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

result.title: No emotional processing required

decisions.title: Evidence from a previous haircut
decisions.situation: Freddie sends you an old photograph. The haircut is difficult to defend. The memory attached to it is much better.

choices.label: Ask for the whole story
Save a copy and label it
Focus entirely on the haircut

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Freddie remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Freddie also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises
decisions.situation: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice
Identify every interruption

result.title: Quiet enough is available
result.body: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive

choices.label: Suggest improving the flavour first

result.title: A review they can use

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in London, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in London.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about
decisions.situation: At a free repair demonstration, a wind-up toy starts smoking. The volunteer explains that it is supposed to do that. The label “DO NOT WIND” drops off its base.

choices.label: Ask what the label means
Step back and let them stop it
Ask whether smoke costs extra

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: Practice grief
decisions.situation: At a free estate-planning demonstration, volunteers act as fictional heirs. Your card says “loving relative”. The person beside you is already asking what the imaginary house is worth.

choices.label: Play the grieving relative sincerely
Ask how real inheritance rules work
Demand the imaginary house in character

result.title: A family worth inventing
result.body: You deliver a moving line about the fictional deceased. The facilitator thanks you. Your neighbour asks whether the line helped your share.

journal.text: I played a grieving relative at an estate-planning demonstration.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: A reminder that needs reminding
decisions.situation: You find a note you wrote to help remember something important. It says only, “The usual one, but different.”

choices.label: Write a clearer private reminder
Work backwards from the context
Assume it will make sense later

result.title: Future you gets better information
result.body: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.

journal.text: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in London needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in London.

decisions.title: Happy statistical decline
decisions.situation: For your birthday, someone sends a list of famous people who had achieved more by your age. They finish with “Hope this inspires you!”

choices.label: Celebrate without the comparison chart
Choose one goal that is actually yours
Read every biography before bed

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version
decisions.situation: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

decisions.title: A number with nowhere to go
decisions.situation: You suddenly remember a telephone number you have not used for years. You cannot remember what you entered a room to fetch, but the number is perfect.

choices.label: Enjoy the memory’s strange priorities
Return calmly to the original task
Treat the distraction as a personal crisis

result.title: An impressive useless recital
result.body: You repeat the number once and laugh at the timing. Memory has supplied an answer to a question nobody asked.

journal.text: I remembered an old telephone number at an unhelpful moment.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: Beginners’ self-defence
decisions.situation: At a free beginner lesson, the instructor asks you to demonstrate a firm “No!” You give one so convincing that a passer-by apologises and leaves.

choices.label: Practise the rest of the lesson
Watch the demonstrations first
Use your new “No!” on the whole lesson

result.title: A useful loud afternoon
result.body: You learn the basics and repeat the shout. The corridor remains unusually clear for the rest of the lesson.

journal.text: I practised the basics at a free self-defence lesson.

decisions.title: Older than bread
decisions.situation: A birthday cake for you arrives with an extra zero among the candles. Someone asks whether you knew the person who invented bread.

choices.label: Ask for the extra candles to be removed
Keep the cake and accept your ancient status
Deliver a speech about surviving the last ice age

result.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing
result.body: They remove the extra candles, then stand back as though they have made you younger. You thank the bakery for its medical breakthrough.

journal.text: I corrected an extra zero on my birthday cake.

decisions.title: You need medical attention

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

Leave before the eulogy

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in London.

List what you did achieve
Send your younger self a furious reply

result.title: The corners remain hostile
result.body: You report that the elastic corners remain a problem. You omit finances; you are not being interrogated by a child with a felt-tip pen.

journal.text: I answered an old note about being wealthy and folding fitted sheets.

decisions.title: Help has been offered

Politely decline and explain your preference
Treat the offer as an insult

result.title: A task shared
result.body: You take the useful part of the offer without treating it as a judgement on everything you can do.

journal.text: I accepted useful help with a small task.

decisions.situation: A younger person points at your outfit and says, “You ate.” You have no food on you. They add, “No crumbs.” This is getting less clear.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.
